title: London → South America
intro: The trip starts with one rule: travel light enough to move fast.
anchor: Leave London with one backpack and no unnecessary “just in case” luggage.
morning: Keep the day easy; sleep as late as practical before the overnight flight.
Final digital check: passports, insurance, cards, offline maps, reservations.
afternoon: Airport with enough buffer to avoid starting the trip stressed.
Eat before boarding rather than rely on airline timing.
evening: Try to sleep on destination time; hydrate aggressively.
eat: Airport meal: functional, not memorable. Save appetite for Buenos Aires.
logistics: Backpack-only is a strategic advantage throughout the solo leg.

title: Buenos Aires
intro: Spring Day. Art. Percussion. Tango. You land and Buenos Aires does not let you ease in.
anchor: La Bomba de Tiempo at Konex on Día del Estudiante / Spring Day, then a real late-night milonga.
morning: ~10:00 land EZE; use official transfer/Cabify/Uber to Palermo.
Drop bag, shower, light porteño lunch. Do not nap for three hours.
afternoon: Palermo + Bosques de Palermo while Spring Day crowds are out.
15:00-17:00 MALBA: 25th anniversary day, free admission; focus on the strongest Latin American work, then leave.
evening: 19:00 doors / 20:00 La Bomba de Tiempo at Ciudad Cultural Konex - exact-date event verified.
Then La Viruta / milonga environment: watch, try, talk to people; no tourist tango dinner.
Home when jet lag wins, ideally ~01:30-02:00.
eat: After Konex: pizza, provoleta or late porteño comfort food.
Drink: Fernet & Coke or vermouth; do not waste first night on a formal tasting menu.
logistics: Konex → Palermo by rideshare at night.
watchOut: Street-phone theft is the practical risk, not a reason to avoid the city. Keep the phone away when not using it; use rideshare between nightlife zones.
sleep: Buenos Aires - Palermo. Hotel shortlist: Mine / Malevo Muraña / 1828 Smart.

title: Buenos Aires
intro: Old-money mausoleums, street-level San Telmo, Boca identity, one of the continent’s great steaks, then tango again.
anchor: Don Julio + a genuinely porteño night, not a sightseeing checklist.
morning: Sleep until ~09:00 after the first night.
Quick El Ateneo / Avenida Santa Fe hit - 20 min, not a pilgrimage.
Fast historic-centre pass: Obelisco / Plaza de Mayo / Casa Rosada exterior.
afternoon: 13:00 San Telmo: eat through the market and Defensa rather than sit for 2 hours.
15:00 rideshare to La Boca; Caminito + Bombonera culture. Stay in tourist core.
evening: 20:00-20:30 serious dinner: Don Julio if booked; El Preferido if not.
Late milonga / La Viruta or an improvised next move with people you have met. Do not impose a 23:00 curfew on Buenos Aires.
eat: San Telmo: choripán / empanada / market grazing.
logistics: Use rideshare San Telmo↔La Boca and after dark.
No football fixture worth distorting the day for on your dates.
watchOut: La Boca beyond the tourist core is not the place to improvise a long solo wander with your phone out.
places: El Ateneo Grand Splendid, Buenos Aires

title: Mendoza
intro: The city disappears behind you; by sunset you are on horseback under the Andes eating asado by a fire.
anchor: Sunset cabalgata + asado + Malbec - the first big landscape pivot of the trip.
morning: Early AEP→MDZ nonstop. Target 08:00-09:30; exact flight to reconfirm before booking.
Hotel bag drop and light lunch.
afternoon: No plaza-ticking. Transfer to the foothills / ranch.
Winter schedule for the current Vempra ride lists ~14:30 departure, 2 hours on horseback and dinner included.
evening: Ride to the viewpoint as the light drops over the Andes.
Asado, wine, dessert and fire-side sobremesa; some departures include guitar.
Return to Mendoza; one drink only if the group continues.
eat: Dinner is part of the horseback experience: asado + wine.
logistics: AEP, not EZE, for the domestic hop.
Sunset ride currently shows free cancellation to 72h and Sep 2026 inventory calendar.
watchOut: You do not need riding expertise, but tell the operator your level. Dress for a cold post-sunset return.
sleep: Mendoza - Casa Lila / Diplomatic / Park Hyatt.
decision: TARGET / RECONFIRM — Earliest useful AEP flight

title: Mendoza
intro: Today is not “visit wineries.” Today is the Andes expressed through wine.
anchor: Valle de Uco + a long lunch at Zuccardi / Piedra Infinita.
morning: Small-group/private-small transfer to Valle de Uco.
One excellent producer in the morning, not three rushed tastings.
afternoon: Long Piedra Infinita lunch with Andes view. Wine is the event; do not schedule a fourth winery.
evening: Simple neighbourhood evening: Fuente y Fonda / local wine bar, no elaborate second tasting menu.
eat: Lunch: Piedra Infinita - flagship food experience.
Dinner: home-style Argentine food, modest portions after a wine day.
logistics: Use a small-group/private-small vehicle; avoid a 40-person coach.
watchOut: If you drank heavily at lunch, the correct evening is water + food + sleep, not proving you can continue drinking.

title: Santiago
intro: Cross the Andes, then taste Chile as geography rather than as a list of sights.
anchor: Boragó: 12-18 preparations built around Chilean ecosystems, after seeing the Andes frame Santiago.
afternoon: Compact city/context hit: central Santiago or Museum of Memory depending energy; keep it to ~90 min.
Late afternoon viewpoint / Cerro San Cristóbal if visibility is good.
evening: Boragó from 17:15 onward. Current Endémica menu CLP 199,000 pp; reserve.
One excellent cocktail/wine after if you still want it; do not dilute the meal with forced clubbing.
eat: Lunch: quick Chilean bite after arrival.
Dinner: Boragó - luxury reset and the city’s defining food experience.
logistics: Stay Providencia for safe, easy late return.
watchOut: Friday afternoons/evenings can see demonstrations in central Santiago. Do not linger around political gatherings; move east for dinner/night.
sleep: Santiago - Le Rêve / Novotel Providencia / Solace.

title: San Pedro De Atacama
intro: By late afternoon the landscape looks extraterrestrial; by night the full moon becomes part of the experience.
anchor: Valle de la Luna sunset + indigenous full-moon astronomy instead of pretending this is a dark-sky night.
morning: Earliest sensible nonstop SCL→CJC. Exact flight to reconfirm; do not lock to an unverified early schedule.
Shared Calama→San Pedro transfer; check in, light lunch, hydrate.
afternoon: Valle de la Luna late afternoon; salt formations and desert sunset.
Keep first day around San Pedro altitude rather than immediately forcing 4,500m.
evening: Alarkapin-style full-moon / Andean astronomy experience: Moon, bright planets/objects, indigenous sky interpretation.
eat: Lunch: La Picada del Indio or similar simple local meal.
Dinner: Adobe / good small Andean kitchen; try llama/quinoa/rica-rica.
logistics: Shared transfer from CJC is the right social/value choice.
26 Sep is full moon - that is a fact shaping the plan, not a problem to hide.
watchOut: Hydrate. Go easy on alcohol. You are about to spend several days above 4,000m.
sleep: San Pedro - Terrantai / NOI Casa Atacama / Tierra Atacama.
places: Valle de la Luna, San Pedro de Atacama
decision: TARGET / RECONFIRM — Then shared transfer to San Pedro
